items.title: Summer
items.text: Summer storms and sudden downpours can overwhelm drainage around homes, while high heat adds stress to HVAC condensation lines and water heaters.

sections.heading: Water Damage Restoration FAQs for Southlake Homeowners

items.q: How quickly should I act after discovering water damage?
items.a: You should contact a restoration team as soon as possible. The longer water sits, the greater the risk to flooring, drywall, and furniture, though the exact outcome depends on the water source and materials involved.

items.q: Will my homeowners insurance cover water damage restoration?
items.a: Coverage depends on your specific policy and the cause of the damage. We provide documentation of our assessment and work to support your claim, but approval and coverage decisions are made by your insurance provider.

items.q: Can all water-damaged materials be saved?
items.a: Some materials, like solid wood furniture or hardwood floors, can often be dried and preserved if treated promptly. Porous materials such as drywall, insulation, and carpet padding usually need to be removed, especially if exposed to contaminated water.
